analysis:
The only change in this PR is a one-line documentation edit at docs/architecture/inference.md:1846, in the sampling-parameters table row for `stop`. The row now says GPT-OSS scopes stop-string matching to the Harmony `final` message (`ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope`, `StopHoldback`), so analysis and tool-call frames never match, and the reported sequence replays the same scope. There are no code, configuration, key, attestation, cache or protocol changes. The patch is complete and the range map is complete.

Security relevance is limited to the described behavior. If implemented as documented, it narrows where user-controlled stop strings can truncate output. This is consumer-supplied input, so ADV-002 could in principle use it to influence output truncation. The scoping reduces the chance that a consumer stop string cuts off tool-call frames or analysis content. It does not touch the T-041 prefix-cache identity, since the sampler and stop settings are not part of cache identity. It does not affect TB-002 encryption of responses (T-008) or the TB-007 inference engine's memory isolation.

The remaining question is whether the code in `ModelEOSPolicy`/`EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift` matches the new text. That source was not supplied, so this review only verified the documentation change and cannot confirm the implementation. It is not a finding, because no evidence shows the doc to be wrong or the behavior to be a regression. If the code change exists in a sibling PR unit, the next pass should check that stop-sequence replay in the reported sequence cannot leak analysis-channel text to consumers. It should also check that the stop-string scope cannot be used to suppress hash or usage accounting.
